newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Well supported at $100/T mark.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Well supported at $100/T mark.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market was steady on Wednesday with support seen at above the $100 mark from a local trader in active trade.

A Singapore trader bought a 20,000-tonne 180-cst cargo from a European major at $100.50 per tonne free-on-board Singapore. Traders said there was an offer from a major for another 20,000-tonne at $102.
"It seems the local trader will continue to bid up the market, so most suppliers just stay on the sidelines waiting for higher prices," said one trader.
Prices were also supported by the recent Taiwan and Indian fuel oil purchase tenders for seasonal demand for the upcoming summer, traders said.
Despite the absence of fresh Chinese enquiries this week, some traders remained optimistic that Chinese demand could emerge soon.
Two Chinese traders emerged late last week to bid for cargoes for delivery southern China.

The 180/380 cst spread widened slightly on strong selling pressure from a European major for 380 cst. The major sold to a Singapore trader a 20,000-tonne cargo loading April 19-23 at $94.50 per tonne.
In the LSWR market, sentiment was bearish with ample supplies while demand was poor, traders said.
An offer for a 100,000-barrel cargo loading from either Singapore or Indonesia was offered at $17.30 per barrel fob with no firm bids seen against it, they said.
Indonesia's 3.6 million barrels allocated in April faced lacklustre demand from Japan and China.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
